description.p: Sonix Studio is a digital audio workstation for Linux, written in Rust with an egui interface. It edits audio directly on the timeline, the way FL Studio does, with magnetic loop snapping — and keeps the engine's word: everything the interface advertises is wired to real DSP, including the parts that are still rough.

ul.li: Timeline arranger with direct clip editing, slicing and magnetic loop snapping
Real-time cpal/ALSA audio engine, with the system's PipeWire working through its ALSA layer
16-step channel rack, piano roll, and touch instruments
Analog Alchemy synthesizer, drum synthesis, per-voice filter and envelope
Multichannel effects mixer with per-track sends, automation lanes and VCA groups
Vocal Studio with microphone recording, a sampler and a pitch-preserving time-stretch
Stem separation (DSP path), a stem focus editor and Suno stem-pack import
Plugin host: catalogues everything, and loads CLAP, VST3 and VST2 effects with delay compensation
Optional AI music assistant speaking to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Export to WAV/MP3/FLAC with the master mix or per-track stems

description.p: Two things are deliberately opt-in rather than shipped: neural stem separation (needs a build with the neural feature plus a user-supplied HTDemucs model — the DSP separator is what runs without one) and LV2 plugin loading, which has no host yet. The project says so itself in its README rather than in a footnote.

ul.li: Real-time cpal/ALSA audio engine, oscillator and drum synthesis, filters with envelopes
Timeline arranger with slicing, magnetic snapping and clip editing
16-step channel rack, piano roll, Vocal Studio and microphone recording
Multichannel effects mixer, master FX chain, delay/reverb and Remix FX
Plugin catalogue for CLAP, VST3 and VST2, with hosting for CLAP/VST3/VST2 effects
Export to WAV, MP3 and FLAC — master mix or per-track stems
